Խունկ — Khunk

Incense in the Armenian tradition

Khunk (խունկ) is frankincense — the fragrant resin of the Boswellia tree — burned on glowing charcoal in a metal censer called a burvar (բուրվառ). In Armenian churches the censer is swung on chains fitted with small bells, and its sweet smoke rises with the prayers of the congregation. In homes, a small burvar is lit for blessing, remembrance, and quiet moments of prayer.

This is a small, quiet corner of the internet in that spirit. Each tap drops grains of resin onto the coals: watch the embers flare, the smoke thicken and curl upward, and listen for the soft crackle.
